name: movements-094
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Trx Single Arm Bicep Curl. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Step 1: Stand comfortably and grasp the handles of the suspension system. Step 2: Lean back resting your weight on one arm, keepng the spine neutral. Step 3: Slowly curl to pull your body weight to the up position. Supinate the arm and squeeze as you approach the end position. Step 4: Lower yourself back down and repeat.

Row 1 column 2: TRX Tricep Extension. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Attach the TRX or other suspension system overhead, having the handles hanging at chest level or slightly lower. Experiment to see what height allows you to set up in the best way. Stand in front of the handles and grab them with your palms facing down. Engage your abs, squeeze your glutes, take a breath and lean forward, lifting your heels off the floor. Keep your elbows straight. Take another breath and lower yourself slowly by bending your elbows. Go down until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle (to the point where your wrists are above your elbows). Hold the position for a moment. Extend your arms by engaging your triceps and bring yourself to the starting position as you exhale.

Row 1 column 3: Tuck Crunch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: To begin, lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your back pressed against the floor. Your arms should be lying across your sides with the palms facing down. Your legs should be crossed by wrapping one ankle around the other. Slowly elevate your legs up in the air until your thighs are perpendicular to the floor with a slight bend at the knees. Note: Your knees and toes should be parallel to the floor as opposed to the thighs. Move your arms from the floor and cross them so they are resting on your chest. This is the starting position. While keeping your lower back pressed against the floor, slowly lift your torso. Remember to exhale while perform this part of the exercise. Slowly begin to lower your torso back down to the starting position while inhaling. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 1 column 4: Tuck L-sit. Equipment: Bench. Exercise guide: The tuck L-sit is a bodyweight hold where you support yourself on parallel bars, parallettes, or the floor with straight arms while pulling your knees toward your chest. Your hips stay lifted, your spine stays tall, and your feet hover off the ground. The goal is to keep your core tight, shoulders depressed, and arms locked out while maintaining the tucked position. It’s a core-intensive, shoulder-stabilizing static hold often used as a progression toward the full L-sit.

Row 2 column 1: Turkish Get-Up. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Starting on back, move to the standing position with dumbbell in one hand. Switch hands between reps.

Row 2 column 2: Two-Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Grab a dumbbell with each arm and place the upper arms on top of the preacher bench or the incline bench. The dumbbell should be held at shoulder length. This will be your starting position. As you breathe in, slowly lower the dumbbells until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched. As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weights up until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard for a second at the contracted position and repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 2 column 3: Two-Arm Kettlebell Clean. Equipment: Kettlebell. Exercise guide: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you raise the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so. Lower the kettlebells back to the starting position and repeat.

Row 2 column 4: Two-Arm Kettlebell Military Press. Equipment: Kettlebell. Exercise guide: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you swing the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so, so that the palms face forward. Press the kettlebells up and out. As the kettlebells pass your head, lean into the weights so that the kettlebells are racked behind your head. Make sure to contract your lats, butt, and stomach for added stability.

Row 3 column 1: Two-Arm Kettlebell Row. Equipment: Kettlebell. Exercise guide: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and then push your butt out as much as possible as you bend over to get in the starting position. Grab both kettlebells and pull them to your stomach, retracting your shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Keep your back straight. Lower and repeat.

Row 3 column 2: Typewriter Pull-ups. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width. Pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar. At the top position, instead of going straight down, shift your body to one side by extending one arm while keeping the other arm bent. Move smoothly from one side to the other, like a typewriter motion, before lowering yourself back down. This exercise increases time under tension and strengthens the lats, biceps, and shoulders while building unilateral pulling strength.

Row 3 column 3: Tyson push-ups. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Starting Position • Feet: Place the soles of your feet flat against a vertical wall, with your toes or balls of your feet on the floor. • Hands: Position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, directly under your lower chest or solar plexus. • Body: Keep your core tight, glutes squeezed, and head in a neutral position. Your knees should hover a few inches above the floor without touching it. Movement Pattern 1. Lower Down: Flex your elbows (tucked around 45 degrees) to lower your chest toward the floor, stopping just a few centimeters short of touching the ground. 2. Rock Back: As you press upward through your arms, push your hips backward and bend your knees, rocking your weight toward your heels while keeping your shins nearly parallel to the floor. 3. Drive Forward: Explode forward from your lower-body/crouched position, shifting your weight back into the starting push-up plank stance to complete the repetition. Key Tips for Proper Form • Keep Knees Low: Do not let your knees or hips pike high up in the air; keep the motion low and horizontal. • Maintain Wall Contact: Keep the soles of your feet pressed against the wall so you don't lose your leverage. • Engage the Core: Avoid arching your lower back by tilting your pelvis backward and bracing your abs.

Row 3 column 4: Upper Back. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Upper Back is suitable for building up the core muscles with a special focus on the deltoid and rhomboid muscles and the upper back muscles

cells.title: Tyson push-ups
cells.guideText:
Starting Position

• Feet: Place the soles of your feet flat against a vertical wall, with your toes or balls of your feet on the floor.
• Hands: Position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, directly under your lower chest or solar plexus.
• Body: Keep your core tight, glutes squeezed, and head in a neutral position. Your knees should hover a few inches above the floor without touching it.

Movement Pattern

1. Lower Down: Flex your elbows (tucked around 45 degrees) to lower your chest toward the floor, stopping just a few centimeters short of touching the ground.
2. Rock Back: As you press upward through your arms, push your hips backward and bend your knees, rocking your weight toward your heels while keeping your shins nearly parallel to the floor.
3. Drive Forward: Explode forward from your lower-body/crouched position, shifting your weight back into the starting push-up plank stance to complete the repetition.

Key Tips for Proper Form

• Keep Knees Low: Do not let your knees or hips pike high up in the air; keep the motion low and horizontal.
• Maintain Wall Contact: Keep the soles of your feet pressed against the wall so you don't lose your leverage.
• Engage the Core: Avoid arching your lower back by tilting your pelvis backward and bracing your abs.
